page: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.2-8 is a flexible compute instance powered by AMD EPYC 7J13 processors based on the x86_64 architecture. The instance configuration allocates 2 physical cores with 2 threads per core, providing 4 dedicated vCPUs operating at a nominal base frequency of 2.55 GHz. System memory totals 8.0 GB, establishing a 2.0 GB per vCPU ratio (1:2 core-to-memory profile).

This virtual machine provision includes no integrated local storage and no hardware GPU accelerators, necessitating remote block storage attachments for persistent file systems. Network configuration includes one complimentary public IPv4 address. The dedicated CPU allocation ensures consistent computational performance without neighbor-induced throttling, though the absence of local NVMe storage requires architectural reliance on network-attached storage latency profiles.

Given its 1:2 vCPU-to-memory ratio, the configuration is cost-efficient for compute-bound operations that do not require extensive memory footprints. Tradeoffs include limited local scratch space and modest aggregate RAM, making this server profile suitable for web servers, API gateways, light continuous integration build workers, and distributed microservices.
description: Oracle Cloud Infrastructure VM.Standard.E4.Flex.2-8 is a compute-focused virtual machine instance built on x86_64 AMD EPYC 7J13 processors running at 2.55 GHz. The instance delivers 4 dedicated vCPUs derived from 2 physical cores with simultaneous multithreading enabled. It includes 8.0 GB of system RAM, maintaining a lean 1:2 vCPU-to-RAM ratio of 2.0 GB per core. The instance features zero local storage, no discrete graphics acceleration, and provisions one complimentary public IPv4 address. The resource profile provides consistent CPU scheduling without noisy-neighbor degradation, representing a cost-efficient option for workloads requiring compute cycles without high memory overhead. Key workload alignments include stateless web services, CI/CD runners, distributed computation tasks, and microservices architectures requiring external persistent storage.
